News.title: Saudi prince found dead in luxury London hotel room after taking cocktail of party drugs
News.content:
PRINCE'S END Saudi prince found dead in luxury London hotel room after taking cocktail of party drugs

A SAUDI prince was found dead in a luxury London hotel after taking a cocktail of party drugs, an inquest heard.

Prince Abdullah bin Fahad bin Abdullah bin Abdulaziz bin Jalawi al Saud, 29, was discovered on the bathroom floor of his £600-a-night room at the Marriott Hotel in Kensington on November 25.



It was found that the young royal had suffered a cardiac arrest after consuming alcohol, the party drug GHB, and other substances.

Inner West London Coroner’s Court heard that the prince arrived at the hotel on November 19 for a week-long stay.



His body was found by a cleaner who had entered his fifth-floor room.

Paramedics were called to the luxury hotel, but sadly he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Following a toxicology test, it was uncovered that Prince Abdullah had a blood alcohol level of 222mg per 100ml of blood.

With almost three times England’s legal drink-drive limit of 80mg in his system, the inquest heard this alone could have caused a coma.

It was also found that he had a fatal level of Gamma-hydroxybutyrate, commonly known as GHB, in his system.

Tests also showed he had traces of cannabis and multiple anti-anxiety medications including Xanax.



The prince has struggled with alcohol misuse and Xanax before his death, the court heard.

He was admitted to the Priory Clinic in Roehampton in south-west London in August last year.

During his stay, he underwent detoxification from alcohol, benzodiazepines and the anti-anxiety drug pregabalin.

Consultant psychiatrist Dr Victoria Chamorro said: “He was assessed as having symptoms of low mood and anxiety on admission.

“When he was discharged he was considered not to be at risk of suicide. He was discharged with a friend but then failed to attend scheduled Zoom appointments.



“Nevertheless there was no concern for him. He engaged well and completed his treatment.”

The inquest heard he was also diagnosed with an upper respiratory tract infection before recovering and leaving the clinic.

Assistant Coroner Jean Harkin said that there was nothing to suggest the prince intended to end his life.

Concluding the inquest, Harkin recorded the death by misadventure, with the medical cause of death given as multi-drug ingestion.

She added: “I would like to offer my sincere condolences to the family of Abdullah.”

News.title: Trump approves landmark nuclear energy deal with Saudi Arabia as Israel fears it could pave way for weapons
News.content:
EASTERN PROMISES Trump approves landmark nuclear energy deal with Saudi Arabia as Israel fears it could pave way for weapons

DONALD Trump has approved a “multi-billion dollar” partnership with Saudi Arabia to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

A major victory for the Kingdom, the agreement will potentially see it enrich its own uranium – marking a shift in longstanding US non-proliferation policy.



This is something that Saudi Arabia has been pushing for years, since the George W Bush administration.

The US Department of Energy hailed the agreement as “historic”, saying that American companies will provide nuclear technology to the country.



The deal consists of an accord under Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, known as a 123 agreement, “alongside an accompanying bilateral safeguards agreement”, a statement said.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said: “These agreements reflect our two nations’ shared commitment to strengthening US-Saudi commercial relations, delivering prosperity at home and security to our allies abroad.”



“Rest assured, these agreements uphold the highest standards of nuclear safety and nonproliferation, while relying on the world’s best nuclear technology and scientists, designed right here in the US.”

The statement further called the deal a “decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership” and said it will now be submitted to Congress for review.

The Trump administration said it will create high-paying jobs in the US, “reinforce global nonproliferation standards”, and deepen the strategic partnership with its ally.

But the deal also has the potential to reshape the power dynamics in the region, where only Israel boasts its own nuclear arsenal.



Israel is expected to oppose it over its objection to a rival nation having nuclear capabilities.

Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett described the pact as a “grave strategic failure that endangers our security.”

Meanwhile, leader of the right-wing opposition Yisrael Beytenu party, Avigdor Lieberman, warned that the civilian nuclear programme will end with nuclear weapons.

He said: “We must all understand that Saudi Arabia’s civilian nuclear program will end in nuclear weapons and lead to a mad arms race across the entire Middle East.

“The State of Israel must make it clear and unequivocal: We will oppose this with all our might.



“The Government of Israel must act with determination before the US Congress to block this move.”

Earlier, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sought to head off emerging criticism, insisting that the US is not going to reach “any agreement with any country in the world that leads to the risk of proliferation.”

The announcement comes as the US President ramps up the war against Iran that aims to wipe out the regime’s ability to develop a nuclear bomb.

But Iran has insisted its nuclear enrichment programme is peaceful.

Ahead of the announcement, Alexander Bollfrass, a nuclear expert at the International Institute for Strategic Studies in London, called the deal “a revolutionary new approach” to nuclear nonproliferation policy.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The revolutionary aspect of this agreement is that the US is not asking Saudi Arabia to abide by the highest possible safeguards, internationally monitored safeguards that are standard and are available today,” he said.

“Instead, it is willing to at least theoretically transfer highly sensitive technology without the same level of oversight that one would expect.”

News.title: Hit and run cop killer jailed for 20 years could be among prisoners released early under Labour reforms
News.content:
COP KILLER EYES FREEDOM Hit and run cop killer jailed for 20 years could be among prisoners released early under Labour reforms

A HIT-and-run cop killer could be among prisoners released early under Labour’s reforms.

Clayton Williams, then 19, was jailed for 20 years in 2016 after striking PC Dave Phillips with a stolen pick-up truck during a high-speed police chase.



The dad of two was thrown into the air and died almost instantly from “catastrophic” injuries in October 2015 at Wallasey, Merseyside.

The officer’s widow, Jen, cried as she read out her victim impact statement and said to cannabis addict Williams in court: “Who gave you the right to play God?”



She added: “I want you to know what you’ve done to me and my daughters.

“Tears flow as I cry myself to sleep every night. It’s soul destroying.



“I have to be strong for the sake of my children. How do I do that, when the children cry for their daddy?”

She said she cannot sleep at night and when she does “she dreams of her husband alive”.

Killers like Williams, who was convicted of manslaughter, currently serve at least two-thirds of their sentences behind bars.

But he may only have to do half of his term due to the Sentencing Act, which is set to kick in from September.



The Ministry of Justice has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Kemi Badenoch set to tell Burnham to ‘get his act together’ and start behaving like the PM in blistering speech
News.content:
KEMI Badenoch will today tell Andy Burnham to “get his act together” and start behaving like the Prime Minister.

The Conservative Party leader will also accuse him of lacking ambition for Britain.



In a blistering speech in central London, Ms Badenoch plans to tear into the Labour PM’s economic plans.

“Andy Burnham needs to do better,” Ms Badenoch will say.



“He is still thinking like the Mayor of Manchester.

“But he is no longer the Mayor of Manchester. He is Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

“He needs to lift his sights. Because the world will not wait for Andy to get his act together.”

She will also call on the PM to prioritise growth and come clean over planned tax rises.

It comes as Labour’s new Prime Minister has been handing out spending commitments like sweeties.

On Monday he announced a £340 million investment to end rough sleeping, on Tuesday he unveiled a £850 million plan to cut energy bills.



And on Wednesday he confirmed a £454million plan to cap bus fares at £2.

He has also signalled further spending on council housing, social care and nationalising utilities.

Ms Badenoch will say: “Andy Burnham needs to rule out tax rises to pay for his spending spree.”

She will also use the speech to tease him over his gimmicky social media videos.

“Andy Burnham seems like a nice guy,” she is expected to say.



“I’ve enjoyed his dodgy dancing and even the shocking revelation that he puts the milk first in his tea. I’m glad he has a sense of humour. It’s needed in this job.”

News.title: There is no reason whatsoever why the early release of criminals should include sex offenders and rapists
News.content:
Soft justice

LABOUR has so far shown a contempt for justice and the victims of crime.

Yes, the Tories shamefully failed to build enough jails during their time in power.



But there is no reason whatsoever why the early release of criminals to reduce prison overcrowding should include sex offenders and rapists.

Why should the comfort of dangerous lags be a greater priority than those living with the everlasting consequence of violence?



The appalling news that two thugs involved in the senseless killing of hero cop PC Andrew Harper could soon be freed was a wake up call.

Andy Burnham was reported to have paused the whole system of emergency early release due to start in September.



But the PM’s priority should always be to put public safety and victims first.

Perhaps he could also end Home Office legal attempts to keep secret the nationalities of foreign criminals.

Why should taxpayers’ money be used to keep them in the dark? Not only is that an affront to democracy.

It will only add more fuel to dangerous accusations of two-tier justice.



Andy’s armada

THE first dozens of small boat migrants broke into Britain on Andy Burnham’s watch.

We’ve heard precious little from our new Prime Minister about what he plans to do about illegal migration.

So far tinkering around the edges — like the one-in-one-out scheme with France — has failed.

There may be signs that French cops are finally starting to get tough on the beaches around Calais.

But realistically, only the windy weather in the Channel has kept illegal migrants at bay in recent weeks.



So will Burnham listen to an enraged public and be bold?

Starting with looking again at a Rwanda-style deportation scheme so recklessly scrapped by his predecessor?

Honest, guv

ANDY Burnham yesterday promised he “would always be honest” with the nation.

He could do with looking at his own tax and spending policies.

It’s a sign of how unprepared for Government his team is that they have made a number of clearly unfunded promises in just the first two days.



Burnham says he is “considering” raising income tax thresholds which will drag 500,000 workers into paying tax for the first time — and 400,000 more into higher brackets.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Months of uncertainty lie ahead until Burnham makes up his mind before what will be another make or break Labour Budget in the Autumn.

He would do better to end Rachel Reeves’s Jobs Tax that has driven up unemployment and killed growth.

News.title: Emergency services rush to popular beach after reports of multiple people in difficulty in water as cops say ‘stay away’
News.content:
EMERGENCY services have rushed to a popular beach after reports of multiple people in difficulty in the water.

Cops and HM Coastguard scrambled to the scene at West Mersea, near Colchester, at around 5.30pm today, with police warning the public to “stay away”.



East of England Ambulance Service are also in attendance, along with Essex Fire and Rescue Service and Essex Police.

In a Facebook post, the force said: “While we remain on scene, we would ask the public to avoid the Seaview Avenue and beach area.



“We appreciate that this will cause some local issues, but would ask for your patience and understanding as we may be there for some time yet.”

The area is known for its strong currents which can take swimmers by surprise.



At least six ambulances, a dozen police cars, a fire engine, a lifeboat, two air ambulances and a Coastguard helicopter were sent to the scene.

One Coastguard truck remained on the shingle beach tonight near an area which was cordoned off with a wind break.



Other emergency vehicles were parked behind a row of multi-coloured pastel beach huts beside the West Mersea Holiday Park.

Two air ambulances landed on the green beside the caravan park’s Sandbanks bar and restaurant while the Coastguard helicopter reportedly landed on the beach.

A lifeboat could be seen launching at one point and searching the water.



Police officers are also searching the shoreline with torches as the light fades.

An eyewitness who lives nearby told The Sun: “I noticed an ambulance come back the house so I went to take a look.

“I could see about 18 emergency vehicles.



“I also saw two air ambulances and one coast guard helicopter which had its door open so they must have been searching for someone.

“On arrival the police had everyone move back and set up a cordon.

“A lot of people had their head in their hands so it was clearly a sensitive issue.

“All the paramedics I could see were down at the beach.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The incident is ongoing and there is no further information at this time with the investigation continues.



An RNLI spokeswoman confirmed its West Mersea lifeboat was launched earlier this evening and its lifeboat from Clacton was also sent to the emergency.

News.title: Burnham should dump the Sentencing Act NOW… length of jail time shouldn’t depend on how many prison spaces there are
News.content:
FIVE minutes into his new job as Secretary of State for Defence and Wes Streeting went on the defensive after being caught on “hot mic” at a gathering of the new Cabinet in the Downing Street garden, joking that the new Justice Secretary Alex Norris “wants to let them all out”.

It was a silly joke to make, even if he thought the microphone was turned off, as surely he knows how sensitive a topic it is when Labour is just about to release killers after they have served just half of their sentences.



This week, the mother of PC Andrew Harper, who ended up being dragged along the road for over a mile by three thugs while investigating the theft of a quad bike, revealed that she has been sent a letter by the Ministry of Justice advising her that two of her son’s killers could soon be released.

They will have served just six and a half years in jail, half of their manslaughter sentences.



Whatever happened to the promise, made when the death penalty was abolished in the 1960s, that life would mean life?

In many cases taking someone’s life now means a short spell in the sin bin before being let out to start all over again.

For PC Harper’s family, including his widow, whom he married just a month before he was killed in August 2019, it really will be a life sentence.

They are never going to get over losing him in such dreadful circumstances. The pain will never go away.

Last night, our new Prime Minister, who wants to retain his popularity ratings, was believed to be considering dumping the Sentencing Act, a bomb which was planted under the justice system by Keir Starmer.

The legislation, which allows the mass release of killers and rapists after serving just half their sentences rather than two-thirds as before, has been sold to the public as a desperate measure to reduce prison overcrowding.



But it is yet one more case of liberal attitudes being forced on society by stealth.

In opposition, Labour backed the campaign for a Harper’s Law, which would guarantee life sentences for anyone killing emergency workers in the course of their duty.

Yet once in power, they let killers of police officers out on the streets instead.

If we are short of prison places, why can’t the Government put its effort into providing more? There was a time when UK governments responded in that way.

Between the mid-1990s, when the then Home Secretary Michael Howard rightfully declared that “prison works”, and 2010 the prison population doubled.



Then, the growth in new places began to stall. In recent years it has been more or less frozen at just under 90,000.

It is as if the Government has decided there should be a fixed quota of criminals, and that prisons, like its failed asylum deal with France, should operate along the lines of one in, one out.

Sorry, but it just isn’t good enough. The length of someone’s jail sentence should depend solely on the seriousness of the crime they have committed, not on capacity constraints of the prison system.



But it isn’t just prison places which are the issue.

Embedded within the criminal justice system are rather too many judges, officials and policy makers who refuse to believe in prison, or even in the principle of punishment itself, and who will take every opportunity which comes their way to water down sentences or keep offenders out of jail altogether.

In their minds, criminals are never truly bad people, it is just that society has mistreated them.

I am all for trying to rehabilitate offenders where possible, but that should never mean shortening sentences.

If murderers are going to come to terms with the pain they have caused they will understand why they need to have their freedom taken away, not plead to be let out.



Thankfully, there is one hopeful sign that the end may finally be in sight for the let-’em-all-out brigade.

Police are investigating Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust for corporate manslaughter for its role in allowing Valdo Calocane out on the street to kill two university students and a school caretaker in 2023.

The paranoid schizophrenic was known to turn violent when he failed to take his medication, yet was freed from a secure hospital regardless.

It was revealed earlier this year that one of the factors was that staff at the NHS trust believed young black men to be over-represented in prisons and secure hospitals.

The result was three innocent people dead, three grieving families — and to turn Calocane from a troubled young man into a killer. That is where hyper-liberal attitudes lead.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now that NHS officials, prison authorities, probation staff and other officials know that they themselves may be held to be complicit in crimes committed by people whom they negligently set free, hopefully we will see a change in practice.

The rights of the public to go about their business without being attacked or murdered might finally get a look in, not just the rights of the criminals.

News.title: Andy Burnham rejects 'point scoring' ahead of key Scotland and Wales talks
News.content:
Andy Burnham rejects 'point scoring' ahead of key Scotland and Wales talks

Andy Burnham will hit the road after his first few days in No10, where he appointed his Cabinet and started rolling out cost of living plans, including a VAT cut on energy bills and the return of the £2 bus fare cap

View 3 Images Andy Burnham says he wants to drive up growth across the country as he travels to Scotland (Image: Lauren Hurley / No 10 Downing Street)

Andy Burnham will dismiss "points scoring" as he seeks to build bridges in Scotland and Wales and get growth firing across the country.

‌



The new Prime Minister will hit the road today after a frenetic few days in No10, where he appointed his Cabinet and started rolling out cost of living plans, including a VAT cut on energy bills and the return of the £2 bus fare cap.

‌



He is expected to hold talks with Scotland’s First Minister John Swinney and Welsh FM Rhun ap Iorwerth, before attending the opening ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Ahead of the visit, he rejected the prospect of "point scoring or discussing constitutional changes like referendums" and said he was focused on practical change.

‌



It comes after Labour was wiped out in Wales in May after more than a century in power, paving the way for Plaid Cymru's leader to become First Minister.

Andy Burnham to bring back £2 bus fare cap slashing travel costs for millions READ MORE :

View 3 Images Andy Burnham and Mayor for the West of England Helen Godwin pose with locals as they take a bus ride during a visit to a bus station in Bath, Somerset (Image: Toby Melville/PA Wire)

The party also suffered its worst ever Holyrood election result, leaving it tied with Reform behind the SNP. The results mean Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are now all governed by nationalist parties.

‌



The Prime Minister said: "When I say we need good growth in every postcode, I mean every postcode across the whole of the UK. Every place and every person matters. I'm not focused on point scoring or discussing constitutional changes like referendums, I want practical measures to help people live well and bring back hope.

“That's why I'm giving families more breathing space with help on the cost of living, which I have started this week by taking VAT off electricity bills, saving money for millions of households."

Mr Burnham is due to meet the First Minister of Northern Ireland, Michelle O'Neill, and Deputy FM Emma Little-Pengelly in August on a summer tour of the UK. The new PM will travel to areas where Labour has been struggling in a bid to win back fed-up voters.

‌



Port Talbot, the steelmaking town in south Wales which lost its final blast furnace in 2024, is believed to be on his itinerary, along with Aberdeen, where the Tories triumphed in a recent by-election amid anger of Labour's oil and gas policy.

View 3 Images It is understood that team Burnham want to maintain momentum over the summer, to avoid repeating some of the mistakes of his predecessor. (Image: Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)

Keir Starmer's first summer in office was dominated by a backlash over the decision to cut the winter fuel allowance and a row over freebies, with the riots following the Southport murders puncturing optimism further.

Article continues below

Last summer, Reform seized control of the news agenda with a drumbeat of announcements on immigration.

It comes as Mr Burnham continues to shape his top team, with Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar expected to get a peerage to serve in the new Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.

Mr Sarwar, who has been Scottish Labour leader since 2021, was the first big figure to call for Keir Starmer to quit in February, pushing the-then PM to the brink. He would stand down as leader and as a Glasgow MSP to sit in the Lords.

News.title: Dramatic footage shows the 'miracle' rescue of two boys who were seconds from death
News.content:
Dramatic footage shows the 'miracle' rescue of two boys who were seconds from death

A mum has praised RNLI volunteers who dashed to save cousins Subby and Kizza after the youngsters got into difficulty in Blackpool, Lancashire, and nearly drowned

Blackpool RNLI crews rescue children from the water underneath pier

This is the dramatic moment two young boys were saved from drowning after a “miracle” rescue at the British seaside.

‌



The extraordinary footage captures the cousins, aged 10 and 12, plucked out of the sea by RNLI heroes. The children were seconds from death after getting into difficulty near a pier in Blackpool, Lancashire.

‌



But RNLI volunteers leapt into action and rescued the boys from the waves, just as the youngest was dragged under the water. He was left “gasping for air” while his cousin clung desperately to the pier.

‌



A terrified mum told how she watched the “nightmare” unfold and pleaded with her 10-year-old son to stay alive: “I knew he’d cling on if he could hear my voice telling him not to let go, but by now the water was rising fast and I could see him going under.”

View 4 Images A 10 year old boy is saved from certain death by the RNLI (Image: RNLI)

The limp body of 10-year-old Subby was dragged into their boat with his arm bleeding from his attempts to hold onto the pier.

‌



In shocking footage, he initially slips from their grasp falling back into the sea until they grab him again. They then went at high speed to rescue of his 12-year old cousin Kizza.

The boys were then taken to the beach to the waiting paramedic while a second lifeboat team went back for an older relative, who'd gone into the sea to help them. He’d been left clinging onto the pier but higher up.

This week, the boy’s mum will return to Blackpool to meet the amazing RNLI rescuers who saved her son and nephew from drowning and has agreed to share their traumatic story ahead of World Drowning Prevention Day on July 25.

‌



View 4 Images The second boy is rescued by the RNLI after clinging onto the pier (Image: RNLI)

Zully, from Leeds, had decided to share their traumatic experience on May 28 during a trip to Blackpool, to warn others of the dangers of the sea and she is backing The Mirror’s Save Lives for Sam water safety campaign.

The terrified mum-of-four told how she tried to wade out to the boys but feared the worst as she watched Subby’s head disappear beneath the water. Her nephew Ted, 21, a carer from Bradford, also tried to reach the boys.

‌



Zully said: “The tide started to come in quickly and I could see the boys in the distance, they were stuck and the water was rising rapidly. A wave whacked me and hit me on the side.

“Ted turned to me and said: ‘Zully, get out, they’re too far out’. I couldn’t go back, as I knew if my son heard my voice, he’d hang on to the pier. I knew he’d cling on if he could hear my voice telling him not to let go, but by now the water was rising fast and I could see him going under.

“It didn’t feel real, it was like I was in some kind of helpless dream - a nightmare. I could see my nephew hanging on, but I could see the fear in his eyes. I could see my boy submerged next to the poles of the pier. I scrambled along the pole and was shouting desperately to him, but I just couldn’t get to him.

‌



“The police came and took me out of the water. I was screaming ‘I can’t get to him - that’s my son and my small nephew.’"

View 4 Images Ted, 21, tried to help his younger relatives after they got trapped by the tide (Image: RNLI)

RNLI praised for saving lives

A 999 call was made by a member of the public, and the Coastguard requested the launch of Blackpool RNLI lifeboat. The volunteer crew were paged for the 11th time in seven days.

‌



The D-class inshore lifeboat was on scene within four minutes.

Zully said: “I was shouting at the top of my voice - we need the orange boat. At this point the boys had been hanging on for 40 minutes. I could see the water going over his head and him gasping for air, but I was struggling to see if he’d come back up again.”

The lifeboat crew immediately located Subby and Kizza and manoeuvred alongside the pier stanchions so the crew could pull the children to safety.

‌



With Ted higher up the pier supports, and a second crew on scene, the original crew made the decision to deliver the children to paramedics waiting on the shoreline.

Zully, who was not aware of the RNLI charity before the dramatic rescue, said she is really looking forward to meeting her family’s rescuers: “God bless these people who came. I can’t comprehend the fact they are just normal people with jobs and their own family, but they’d risk that to save my family.

“The crew were all living in that moment, they had no concern for all those people watching and everything going on around them. They went in there with a job to do. They don’t get enough credit for what they do. Nothing mattered to those people in that boat but saving lives and that’s incredible.”

‌



Save Lives For Sam

'The sea can be evil'

Zully had travelled to Blackpool during the May half term with her sister, sister-in-law, and her son Ted, along with their children to celebrate Eid al-Adha.

They had checked the tide online ahead of their impromptu trip, but tide times and heights vary throughout the month and the incoming tide can easily leave people stranded.

‌



Zully continued: “When I saw Subby coming in on that lifeboat and being carried away, it was like a miracle. I thought he’d gone.

“He survived because of these people who are volunteers. It was like a dream come true. I’m a single mum and I do my best for them. I was beating myself up thinking what more could I have done. I’d checked the tide but never expected things to happen so quickly.”

Zully added: “The sea can be evil, it doesn’t care who you are, it just takes you. I keep my son so close now, it’s shaken us all. This happened to the people I love and it could so easily happen to other families too.

‌



“I have been reliving that moment and keep seeing the people in that orange boat and the marvellous care they gave doing exactly what they are trained to do. They just want to save people for no rewards and that’s just amazing.

“Without the RNLI, I would have lost him. My first boy. I’d have never forgiven myself. Not only that I was the one in charge of the other children. I could never have carried the guilt of going on if it would have been another outcome. The guilt would have eaten me.

“We didn’t even know who these rescuers were before, but now I know they are volunteers and the RNLI is a charity. I'd urge people to support them. They do what they do even thinking once about their own lives, what an incredible selfless act.”

‌



View 4 Images The RNLI works around the clock to keep us safe (Image: Loop Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

'Remember to float if you're in difficulty'

Chris Cousens, RNLI Water Safety Lead said: “We are incredibly grateful to Zully and her family for their courage in speaking up about their experience to ensure others are mindful of the risks.

“Nobody visits the coast expecting to get into difficulty. We’re urging families to check the tide times before you go. If you can’t understand the information on tide tables, ask people who know the area and pay attention to any safety signs.

Article continues below

“Always carry a means of calling for help, like a fully charged mobile phone. If you do get into difficulty, call 999 and ask for the Coastguard.

“Instinctively, most people who find themselves struggling in the water will begin to panic, swim, or thrash about. We’re urging people to ignore this instinct and remember to float: Tilt your head back, with your ears submerged. Relax and try to breathe normally.

"Move your hands and legs to help you stay afloat if you need to. It’s fine if your legs sink – we all float differently. By doing this, you give yourself the chance to rest and recover your breathing. Once you’ve regained control of your breathing, you can call for help or swim to safety.”

News.title: 'Andy Burnham should listen to Gary Lineker and company — and tax their wealth'
News.content:
'Andy Burnham should listen to Gary Lineker and company — and tax their wealth'

Andy Burnham swept into No 10 this week and charged his new Cabinet with "getting that cost of living down" — and now 120 millionaires, including Gary Lineker, have urged him to tax their wealth

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

While Britain's poorest scrape to survive, more than 100 of its richest do something extraordinary today: Demand the government take more of their money.

‌



Collectively, these millionaires have written to Andy Burnham with a message so blunt it should burn through every excuse politicians have hidden behind for a generation - tax us.

‌



Not the care worker on her third shift. Not the pensioner rationing the heating. Not the family surviving on food bank parcels. The millionaires. The people whose wealth quietly breeds more wealth, while millions work themselves hollow just to make ends meet.

‌



New PM Andy Burnham announces VAT cuts on household electricity bills from October READ MORE :

A two per cent tax on wealth above £10 million could raise £24 billion. Equalising capital gains tax with income tax brings in another £12 billion.

These are not radical numbers conjured from thin air. This is money sitting, growing, compounding - in accounts belonging to people who have looked at their own fortunes and said out loud: I do not need this much.

Britain has 157 billionaires

Their combined wealth now equals more than a fifth of the entire country's GDP. A fivefold increase since 1990. And while those fortunes have ballooned beyond any sane definition of need, healthy life expectancy in the UK has collapsed, down two years in a decade, now under 61.

‌



The sixth-largest economy on the planet ranks second-to-last among comparable wealthy nations in years lived in good health.

People are dying younger

People are dying younger in a country awash in millionaire and billionaire money. It is not misfortune. Nor is it a political choice made over decades, and it demands a political answer now. The reality of modern Britain is stark. Median household income stands at £38,900, yet a family of four needs £88,000 simply to live comfortably outside London.

That leaves the average household surviving on less than half the income required for genuine security. Not to live extravagantly. Not to feel wealthy. Simply to pay the bills, withstand an unexpected expense and face the future without fear.

Article continues below

How much does one person actually need?

Yet individual wealth has reached such grotesque levels that it has severed all connection to human reality. So ask yourself: how much does one person actually need?

Mr Lineker and those beside him have answered that with more courage than most politicians manage in a lifetime.

The Prime Minister should listen. Tax vast fortunes. Rescue public services. Give Britain back some decency.

News.title: Six key points about UK wealth tax - including how money could be used
News.content:
More than 100 UK-based millionaires - including former Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker - have signed a letter urging new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to tax their wealth.

The letter - organised by the group Patriotic Millionaires UK - says: “We want you to tax us. We can afford it. We’re not talking about higher taxes on those who get up and go to work for their income every day, but on the very richest whose income is derived from the wealth they hold.”

But just what is a wealth tax and what’s the chances of the UK introducing one?

Andy Burnham to bring back £2 bus fare cap slashing travel costs for millions READ MORE :

View 4 Images Former England star and Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker has joined fellow millionaires calling for a wealth tax (Image: Netflix)

‌



What is proposed?

Patriotic Millionaires, the group Tax Justice UK and others are proposing an annual 2% tax on wealth above £10million. Tax Justice UK says it would affect around 20,000 people in the UK – fewer than 0.04% of the population.

View 4 Images Former City trader Gary Stevenson is among vocal backers of a wealth tax (Image: Rob Parfitt / Channel 4)

It’s not the only one suggested, however. The Unite union put forward a one-off “emergency” 1% wealth tax on the assets of the super-rich. It would apply to individuals with fortunes exceeding £4million which, it claimed, would generate approximately £25billion per year. Doing so could “help fund pay increases for public sector workers to fill the more than 100,000 vacancies in the NHS.”

The Green Party proposed a wealth tax of 1% annually on assets above £10million, and of 2% on assets above £1billion. It has also called for reform of capital gains tax to align the rates paid by taxpayers on income and taxable gains.

‌



Those behind a 2% wealth tax on assets over £10million also back the same overhaul of capital gains tax, claiming it would raise a further £12billion.

How would it be collected?

That’s one of the key questions that supporters of a wealth tax need to address given criticism that it’s hard to impose.

This is Tax Justice UK’s answer for its proposal: “Like inheritance tax, it would involve a self-declaration of asset values by the taxpayer, backed up by a compliance team at HMRC. HMRC could also further develop registers of assets. This would help crack down on dirty money too.”

How much could a 2% wealth tax raise?

Those behind the proposal claim it could rake in £24billion. To put that into context, calculations by the Office for Budget Responsibility suggest increasing the UK’s defence spending to 3% of GDP will demand an additional £17.3billion per year by 2029/30. It could also fund the equivalent of 600,000 NHS nurses.

‌



View 4 Images Property could firm part of the assets of the super rich that form part of a wealth tax (Image: VICKIE FLORES/EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock)

Will a wealth tax raise that much?

That is another of the big debates, which sceptics suggesting it would raise much less, potentially considerably less.

Nailing down and properly assessing what the super-rich own is a challenge in itself but, critics argue, getting them to cough up so much more is another matter. The argument has always been that, if they’re that wealthy, they can employ the best accountants and tax experts to find loopholes, or simply more their wealth elsewhere.

This question of whether the rich would just up sticks and move abroad is hotly contested, especially amid claims there would be an exodus. However, it is certainly true that if a small number of, say, billionaires left then it risks leaving a hole in the tax raising plan.

‌



A report by the independent Wealth Tax Commission in 2020 concluded that “an annual wealth tax is a non-starter in the UK”, adding “we should fix our existing taxes on wealth instead.” However, it did suggest a one-off that could “raise one-quarter of a trillion pounds over five years.”

Gary Stevenson, a former City trader and signatory of the Patriot Millionaires’ letter, clashed with leading tax expert Dan Neidle while making the case for a wealth tax in a recent Channel 4 film.

Mr Neidle branded the 2% tax proposal “absolute populist claptrap and the people pushing this would be ashamed of themselves.”

What other countries have a wealth tax?

Dan Neidle points out how, in 1990, there were 12 wealth taxes in Europe – now there are only three: Spain, Norway and Switzerland.

‌



Spain’s version, for example, starts at 1.7% on those with a net worth €3million, rising to 3.5% on assets over €10m. However, it contains generous exemptions.

The Norwegian wealth tax applies at 1% on assets above about £140,000, with an additional 0.1% above £1.6million. The Swiss models varies considerably between cantons .

Is a wealth tax likely to happen?

Firstly, those backing the proposal say it has huge public support. A YouGov survey from early 2025 found 75% of just over 4,100 people asked said they were strongly or somewhat supportive of a 2% wealth tax on wealth above £10million.

All eyes are now on Andy Burnham and new Chancellor John Healey. In an interview with Gary Lineker, Mr Burnham refused to rule it out, suggesting his incoming government may have “to ask for a little more” tax at some point. But he also added that he wanted to focus on “bringing people together” rather than creating “new divisions”.

News.title: MS breakthrough as NHS offers first pill to help sufferers walk
News.content:
MS breakthrough as NHS offers first pill to help sufferers walk

The NHS is offering a new pill called fampridine, which boosts nerves damaged by multiple sclerosis (MS) to help electrical messages travel more effectively to muscles

View 3 Images Some MS patients can have problems walking (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A new pill is being offered by the NHS to help people with multiple sclerosis (MS) walk more easily.

‌



Thousands of patients in England will now be eligible for the “life-changing” drug fampridine, which acts like a “signal booster” for nerves damaged by MS, helping electrical messages travel more effectively to the muscles.

‌



The twice-daily pill will be offered to around 5,000 patients who until now have only been offered physiotherapy, walking aids or devices to support their feet.

‌



Ceri Smith, head of policy and evidence at the MS Society, said: "We're delighted that fampridine has now been approved for use on the NHS.

View 3 Images Patients take two fampridine pills daily

"Over 120,000 people live with MS in England and Fampridine is the only licensed treatment that helps improve walking ability and speed for some of these people. For many of them, it's life-changing, allowing them to live more independently or stay in employment.”

‌



MS is an incurable autoimmune disease which affects the brain and spinal cord. Symptoms can include tiredness, dizziness, tingling in different parts of the body, muscle cramps, vision problems and memory problems.

View 3 Images Fampridine helps electrical messages travel along nerves damaged by MS (Image: Getty Images/DisabilityImages)

Fampridine has a list price of around £4,700 per patient per year, however the collective bargaining power of the NHS means it has negotiated a confidential discount.

‌



Professor Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, said: "Walking difficulties can have a huge impact on the freedom and independence of people with MS, so this signal-boosting pill could be life-changing for thousands of patients.

"Fampridine helps electrical messages travel along nerves damaged by MS, giving people the chance to walk more easily and helping them be more mobile to do more of the everyday things that matter to them.

"For some, even a modest improvement could mean getting around the house more easily, going out with greater confidence and living more independently."

‌



What is Multiple Sclerosis?

MS patients are scored on the extent of their disability and those rated between four - able to walk without an aid or rest for around 500 metres - and seven - patients who use wheelchairs or are unable to walk further than five metres - will be offered fampridine.

Patients will try the drug for two to four weeks, with walking ability assessed before and after treatment. Those who show progress will continue to take the medicine and will be reviewed regularly. Fampridine trials found the drug improved walking speed in 43% of patients and helped people walk for longer.

Article continues below

Aysen Slack, 65, from Eastbourne, previously paid for fampridine privately, but stopped due to costs. She said: "Fampridine seemed to be working well for me, but paying for the medication was a significant expense and I could not keep doing that forever. So I had to make the difficult decision to stop taking it.

"I would definitely like to try fampridine again on the NHS. My mobility has decreased a lot and even in my flat I have to use sticks now. It would make a huge difference to my life if I were able to improve my walking."

Ceri Smith added: "It's vital that MS services now have the support they need to make fampridine available to all people with MS who could benefit from it, regardless of where in England they live."

News.title: Gary Lineker among 120 millionaires urging new PM to make them pay more tax
News.content:
Gary Lineker among 120 millionaires urging new PM to make them pay more tax

In a letter to Andy Burnham - organised by the Patriotic Millionaires group - they say: 'As millionaires we have a clear message for you, our new Prime Minister: tax us'

View 4 Images Former Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker says: 'I’m proud to stand with people across the UK who want to live in a more equal society' (Image: PA)

Gary Lineker has joined more than 100 UK-based millionaires calling on new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to tax their wealth.

‌



In a letter to the Labour leader - organised by the Patriotic Millionaires group - they say: "As millionaires we have a clear message for you, our new Prime Minister: tax us. We are proud to pay and here to stay. We’re not talking about higher taxes on those who get up and go to work for their income every day, but on the very richest whose income is derived from the wealth they hold.”

‌



Signatories include former England striker Lineker alongside Ian Gregg, the former chairman of the sausage roll chain Greggs, and film director Richard Curtis - behind hits including Love Actually and Notting Hill.

‌



Others include the Scottish author Val McDermid, former City trader and economist Gary Stevenson, and climate expert and author Michael Berners-Lee, whose brother was the inventor of the internet.

Hope for income tax cut for lower earners as Burnham prepares cost of living blitz READ MORE :

View 4 Images Love Actually film director Richard Curtis is among the 120 millionaires to sign letter to Andy Burnham (Image: Variety via Getty Images)

Former Match of the Day presenter Lineker, who added his name to the letter of 120 millionaires, said: “Our fantastic country deserves all of us to get behind it. I’m proud to stand with people across the UK who want to live in a more equal society.”

‌



He added: “Paying your fair share is a basic British value, but so many ordinary people are already paying more than they can afford. Our richest people can do more and most want to. To live up to our national values our new government must raise taxes on extreme levels of wealth for a fairer, better, more hopeful Britain.”

There are various forms of wealth taxes, but Patriotic Millionaires claim a 2% tax on the assets of the super-rich over £10million could raise £24billion for the Treasury.

Just a tiny proportion of the population would also be hit by the move - fewer than 0.04% or around 20,000 people, according to Tax Justice UK. Previous research for The Mirror has also found a wealth tax on the 350 wealthiest families alone - including 156 billionaires - could raise a whopping £15billion.

‌



A tax on wealth could cover over a third of the total core schools budget in England, which stood at around £65billion in 2025-2026. It could also cover an extension of free school meals to all school-aged children in England, with plenty of cash left over. Research from the Child Poverty Action Group in 2023 found this would come at a cost of £2billion-per-year to the taxpayer.

It would be more than enough to end the housing benefit freeze - £1.5billion annually - that charities have blamed for leaving people on the breadline. Separately, it would be more than enough to plug the entire funding gap in defence spending of £4.7billion while helping the UK reach 3% of GDP spending by 2029-30, which would cost between £13 billion and £17 billion per year.

Before entering No10 earlier this week, Mr Burnham did not rule out a wealth tax in an interview with Lineker. The new Labour leader said: “I’m not going rule things out right now. I do believe we need a greater sense of fairness and people feeling that things are being done in the right way and a fair way.

‌



View 4 Images Crime author Val McDermid (Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC/Firecrest Films/Claudia Massie)

“But at the same time, you know, I don’t want to sort of be perceived as somebody who’s coming in with grudges and agendas and, you know, going to just immediately find or demonise one group or create a new way of dividing people.”

He added at the time: “And at some point that might be having to ask for a little more. But, you know, those decisions are not for now. They’re for another day.”

‌



Patriotic Millionaires adds that equalising capital gains tax - the levy paid on profits made on the sale of an asset - with income tax could also bring in £12billion.

Wes Streeting, who was appointed Defence Secretary earlier this week, called for this measure when he quit Keir Starmer’s Cabinet in May, saying it was a “wealth tax that works”.

Such a move is unlikely to breach Labour’s manifesto, which pledged to protect working people from hikes to VAT, national insurance and income tax.

‌



But Jonathan Reynolds, the current Business Secretary, dismissed the idea of a wealth tax as “daft” in 2025.

View 4 Images Former City trader and economist Gary Stevenson has signed the Patriotic Millionaires letter (Image: Ben Birchall/PA Wire)

He added at the time Labour had already imposed taxes on wealthy Brits, saying: “This Labour Government has increased taxes on wealth as opposed to income – the taxes on private jets, private schools, changes through inheritance tax, capital gains tax.”

‌



Critics of a wealth tax have argued the introduction of levy would result in the super-rich fleeing the country to avoid the extra costs of living in Britain. While some would likely leave, there appears to be little concrete evidence to point to a potential mass exodus of millionaires.

Instead, recent research by Patriotic Millionaires by Survation found 75% would be be willing to pay more tax to help protect and strengthen the social, cultural and economic foundations they value in Britain.

But the UK-based millionaires who have signed the letter organised by Patriotic Millionaires add: “Extreme wealth sitting idle in the hands of a few can be put to work: reducing inequality, investing in sustainable jobs, strengthening hospitals, schools and social care, supporting entrepreneurs with the skills and infrastructure they need, and giving small businesses access to affordable finance.

‌



“Our wealth is our country’s secret weapon - let’s get serious about using it.

“There are a few people left with outdated economic thinking and few others desperate to hold onto every penny they can. But they are a minority. Those that can’t see past the end of their own self interest have no place in designing a Britain for the future.”

Julia Davies, member of Patriotic Millionaires UK, added: “This is a fresh opportunity for our country. A chance for the Prime Minister to help rebalance power, reduce the shocking levels of wealth inequality which intensifies the cost of living crisis, and raise much-needed revenue for our public services, improving life for everyone.

Article continues below

“We millionaires are here to be taxed more and we urge our new PM to grab this opportunity with both hands and tax our wealth."
